html:
In 1972 French scientists found that uranium ore from the Oklo mine in southeast Gabon had once worked as a natural nuclear reactor, about two billion years ago.

Workers in France noticed that ore from the mine had slightly too little of the fissile isotope uranium-235. Study showed that groundwater had let chain reactions of nuclear fission run on and off for long periods in several places in the deposit.

Oklo is the only known example on Earth. It is used to test whether the constants of physics have changed over time, and to study how waste from reactors moves in rock over very long spans. The mine at Mounana was one of the uranium sources of French nuclear power from 1961 until it closed in 1999.
sum: In 1972 French scientists found that uranium ore from the Oklo mine in southeast Gabon had once worked as a natural nuclear reactor, about two billion years ago.
